fleet.where: Docker 29.1.3 in WSL 2 (kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) on one laptop
fleet.image: python:3.12-slim (sha256:aa943ce4...) + openssh-server; Python 3.12.16 in the containers
fleet.per_container: own hostname and random /etc/machine-id; sshd with root login by key only
fleet.key: throwaway ed25519 key made by `up` in the fleet directory and deleted by `down`
fleet.hub: WSL 2, Python 3.12.3, Bitcoin Core 31.1.0 (/root/opt/bitcoin-31.1/bin/bitcoind); the relay party runs locally on the hub
fleet.command: python3 -m bitvm_corpus native run --track bitvm3-setup $(cat FLEET/hosts.args) --ssh-config FLEET/ssh_config

runs.network: tc netem `delay 40ms 10ms loss 0.5%` on every container's eth0 and on the bridge (both directions)

not_shown: The containers share the laptop and the WSL 2 kernel: they are separate hosts on a network, not separate physical machines.
netem stands in for a wide-area network: delay, jitter and loss on one bridge, with no real routing, congestion or NAT.
The hub and Core run on the same VM as the containers.
